content: For dense nuclei regions where single-cell segmentation fails, accepted alternatives to per-nucleus counting are: (1) percent-area / fractional-area-above-threshold (binary mask of positive-channel signal within a DAPI+ region mask, expressed as % area), (2) integrated optical density (IOD) within a region ROI, (3) pixel-based colocalization coefficients (Manders M1/M2 measure fraction of one channel's above-threshold pixels that overlap another channel's above-threshold pixels — but Manders overlap coefficient itself is now discouraged in favor of Manders' split coefficients or Pearson's r for interpretability), (4) semi-automated FIJI macros for dense cytoplasmic/nuclear counting (e.g. pancreatic islet beta-cell density tools) as a middle ground when full segmentation isn't reliable. Caveat: none of these directly yield a per-cell double-positive count; they estimate co-expression as area/intensity fraction, so they should be reported as a distinct, parallel metric (not substituted into per-cell % double-positive statistics).
